name: Martinus Legionensis
evidence: Multiple searches for Martin of León's Liber Sermonum and biblical commentaries returned no English translation results. Academic articles reference the work in Latin only; Documenta Catholica Omnia provides Latin text.

name: Remigius Antissiodorensis
evidence: Searches for Remigius of Auxerre's commentaries on Vergil, Boethius, biblical texts, and Martianus Capella found no English translations. Wikipedia and encyclopedia entries confirm his prolific commentary writing but mention no English versions.

name: Zacharias Chrysopolitanus
evidence: Searches for Zacharias Chrysopolitanus (d. 1155) and his Unum ex quattuor (Gospel harmony) found no English translation. Work exists in Latin manuscripts and PL 186:11-620 only.

name: Ekkehardus Uraugiensis
evidence: Internet Medieval Sourcebook contains English translations of portions of Ekkehard of Aura's works, including 'Hierosolymita and World Chronicle (On the Crusades)'. However, full Chronicon universale does not appear to be completely translated.

name: Robertus Pullus
evidence: Robert Pullen's Sententiarum Theologicarum Libri Octo (12th c. theological compendium) found no English translation in searches. Only Latin editions via Patrologia Latina (Dom Mathoud, 1655 edition) and scholarly references to the Latin text.

name: Garnerius Lingonensis
evidence: Garnerius Lingonensis (Bishop of Langres, d. 1198) and his Sermones in festa Domini et Sanctorum found in PL 205 only. No English translation located in comprehensive sermon searches.

name: Taio Caesaraugustanus
evidence: Searches reference recent critical editions (Brepols 2023, Aguilar Miquel ed.) in Latin and Spanish. Earlier searches mention possible English translations in critical editions but specific details not verified. Corpus Christianorum in Translation may include excerpts.

name: Hariulfus Aldenburgensis
evidence: Hariulf's History of St Riquier is the first authoritative English translation of Hariulf's Latin Chronicon Centulense by Kathleen Thompson. Published Manchester University Press, 2024, in Manchester Medieval Sources series (ISBN 978 1 5261 5410 1).

name: Joannes diaconus (Hymonides)
evidence: John the Deacon's biography of Pope Gregory the Great (9th c.) found in multiple references but no modern English translation located. Manuscript editions only in Patrologia Latina (PL LXXV, 50 sqq) and Acta Sanctorum.

name: Smithius, Joannes
evidence: John Smith (18th c. Bede editor) Annotationes are editorial apparatus in Latin, not a medieval authorial corpus. Not a realistic translation target per claim notes. Modern English editions of Bede's own works exist, but not of Smith's annotations.

name: Joannes Bezuensis
evidence: Jean/Joannes Bezuensis (Jean of Beze, d. 1120) and his Chronicon Besuense of Beze Abbey found no hits in English translation searches. Not located in English translation resources or medieval source databases.

name: Bonifacius Moguntinus
evidence: Saint Boniface (Bonifacius Moguntinus, c. 675–754) letters extensively translated into English. Multiple editions: Ephraim Emerton's The Letters of Saint Boniface (Columbia University Press, first published 1940, republished 2000). Also available via Internet Archive and Fordham Internet History Sourcebooks.

name: Hugo de S. Maria Floriacensis
evidence: Hugh of Fleury's Historia ecclesiastica (4 or 6-volume ecclesiastical history to 855 CE) found no English translation. First print edition 1638 (Rottendorf); selections in Patrologia Latina CLXIII. Latin editions only.

name: Hugo Pictavinus
evidence: Hugo Pictavinus (d. 1167) Historia, sermons, theological treatises found no English translation in comprehensive medieval sermon and theological text searches.

name: Zacchaeus Christianus
evidence: Zacchaeus Christianus's Consultationes Zacchaei et Apollonii (4th c. Christian-pagan apologetic dialogue) found no English translation. Modern French translation exists (Feiertag & Steinmann, Paris 1994) but no English version located.

name: Philastrius Brixiensis
evidence: Philastrius of Brescia's Diversarum hereseon liber (c. 384, catalogue of 128 Christian and 28 Jewish heresies) found no English translation. Polish translation mentioned in claim notes; Latin text available via Perseus and Internet Archive, but no English version.

name: Gerardus Itherius
evidence: Gérard Ithier (7th prior of Grandmont, 1188–1198) and his Speculum Grandimontis found minimal search results. Life of Stephen of Muret mentioned but unclear if Gerardus Itherius's specific compilation has been translated to English.

name: Valerianus Cemeliensis
evidence: Valerianus Cemeliensis (Valerian of Cimiez, 5th c.) and his De bono disciplinae found no English translation. Work exists in disputed authorship, appears in PL XL 1219-22, LII 691-6, and CCSL 78 (1958). Latin editions only.

name: Alanus Antissiodorensis
evidence: Alan of Auxerre (Alanus Antissiodorensis, Bishop 1152–1167) wrote Vita of Bernard of Clairvaux but no direct English translation of his specific work located. Bernard's vita exists in multiple translations (William of Saint-Thierry, Arnold of Bonneval, Geoffrey of Auxerre), but Alan's version not specifically verified as translated.
